verdict.rationale: Supabase documents Edge Functions as server-side TypeScript functions distributed globally, and markets them as custom code you write "without deploying or scaling servers." The docs show HTTP invocation, with cron jobs making an HTTP request to an Edge Function, and several first-party deploy paths (MCP `deploy_edge_function`, AI Assistant). However, SDK/client-library invocation of functions is not evidenced, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: documented SDK/client-library invocation of functions, an explicit CLI deploy workflow for functions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy server-side functions invoked by HTTP or SDK calls without managing servers

citations.quote: Edge Functions are server-side TypeScript functions, distributed globally at the edge—close to your users.
Easily write custom code without deploying or scaling servers.
make an HTTP request, such as invoking a Supabase Edge Function
You can also use Supabase's AI Assistant to generate and deploy functions automatically.
